title: The frontier model's answer as a display-only second opinion: are its confident names as safe as the product's, and does taking its first choice only where it states at least 0.5 put the right group first more often than the model alone, on the confirmation set?
status: registered 2026-11-11 and revised 2026-11-12 after an independent review of the code and this file, before anything ran; the set is not built. Every step needs the product owner's go
request: the product owner chose (2026-11-11) to add the frontier model's answer to the product as a display-only second opinion, never a gate, and to test it on the confirmation set. This file registers that test before the set exists and limits what its result may change.
background: docs 21.3.28-21.3.31. On the first fresh set (development data) GPT-5.6 Sol's names at a stated probability of at least 0.99 were all right (17 of 17 at the strict reading, 8 of 8 at the behaviour reading) and taking the model's first choice where it states at least 0.5 put more reports first than either system (29 and 28 of 44). The test of 2026-11-02 on new reports (llm_confidence_cutoff_2026-11-02) had 12 known reports: 6 confident names, none wrong; switch 10 of 12 first, the model 8, the product 4. That is below its registered 30 and descriptive only. No registration covers a display-only use.
question: On vendor reports published from 2026-11-03 on, after GPT-5.6 Sol's knowledge cutoff, not cited by ATT&CK and in no other set: (1) are the model's names at a stated probability of at least 0.99 as safe as the product's names, with at least as many right; (2) does the model's first choice where it states at least 0.5, else the product's leader, put the right group first more often than the model alone; (3) do both hold for the call the product's button makes?
role: test set: evaluation only, never tuned on, never a training or calibration set; local only (the text belongs to each vendor; CISA advisories are US government works); not redistributed. The fresh set of 2026-10-28 (the cut-offs were chosen on it) and the second fresh set of 2026-11-02 (the descriptive test) are development data for this question. The decisive set of 2026-11-04 cannot serve it: its window lies inside the model's training period
made_before: any system (the product or a model) ran on any post of the window, the set is built, or any post of the window was sampled or inspected. On 2026-11-12 the store's last listing was still that of 2026-11-09; no post of the window was opened. The store's own rules read every stored post as data

set.definition: the confirmation set as registered in knowledge_store_decisive_2026-11-04 ('confirmation_set'): posts published from 2026-11-03 on, collected by the store refresh and built the same way (scripts/prepare_fresh_reports.py --list --from-store with its own window, every URL an earlier listing or set considered left out; for this set's own second freeze see 'looks'), with its own label review before any run; scored on its own, never pooled with the fresh sets or the decisive set
set.shared_with: store text waits for the same set (store_text_lead_rule_2026-11-10, knowledge_store_decisive_2026-11-04). A store-text question on this set is registered on its own before the set's first run. The product's code, defaults and commit (store members off) are common to both questions, but the product runs are not: the store-text question makes its own runs (behaviour with --mask-store-names, and strict), because scripts/store_text_lead.py refuses a behaviour run without the store-name masking and the registered model runner cannot read that masking. Neither question changes its rule after seeing the other's result
set.builder: scripts/prepare_fresh_reports.py (sha256 79ad81449207357f3d292ce388f27c1fed20463517fa09ef44303794b7fa4af1 today; the hash at the freeze is recorded in an amendment). Labels and masking as for the fresh sets: label_report on the post as reported, every actor name (ATT&CK and the MISP threat-actor list) and vendor cluster code becomes 'the adversary', at most 8 reports per actor, one copy of a cross-post, retellings of a report of another set left out. Posts shown in a session before this registration, or later outside this set's own build, label review and runs, are left out (--shown, from a scan of every session transcript, as for the decisive set). The ATT&CK release and the MISP list used are recorded at the freeze
set.label_review: before any system runs, every known and open-set report is read against the vendor's own attribution; a report whose label disagrees, that attributes to several actors or to none, or that is a roundup is excluded, never relabelled (the set's amendments.json, frozen with it). This review is the only reading of the window's posts
set.collector: make store-update, run by hand; a run at least every 60 days loses nothing (docs/KNOWLEDGE_STORE_DESIGN.md). Expected at 4-7 usable known reports a month: 30 by about March-June 2027, 60 by mid-2027 to early 2028
set.looks: two, each on the set as frozen then: the first when it holds 30 known reports after review (as registered for the set; descriptive only), the second when it holds 60 (the store programme's small-set rule: below 60 nothing is adopted). The second freeze re-lists the whole window from 2026-11-03: this set's own first listing is never passed to --exclude-listed, and the first look's label-review exclusions stay. The second look scores every report of the set as frozen then, the first look's included, so the two looks are not independent; first-look reports that the cap of 8 per actor drops at the second freeze are reported by count, and their first-look results stand. No rule, cut-off, prompt or masking changes between the looks; a change after the first look turns the reports of that look into development data and only later reports count

arms.product: the product's defaults at the commit recorded at the freeze, local pipeline (no API key, local LLM off, technique head service on): scripts/attribution_benchmark.py --report-set fresh --cti-hal <reports.jsonl> --open-set <open_set.jsonl> --report-observations 0, once with --anonymize behavior and once with --anonymize names
arms.model_registered: openai/gpt-5.6-sol through OpenRouter (stated knowledge cutoff 2026-02-16, before the window), reasoning effort medium, one call per report, the prompt and schema of scripts/fresh_llm_attribution.py (sha256 365dc81f6c7456ebadc95455b69d3d5a3737157fc37915374603eed176a102f2), --level behavior: the statements the product reads, with malware, tool and operation names hidden as well. Unchanged from the test of 2026-11-02
arms.model_as_shipped: the call the product's button makes: apt_classifier.model_opinion.ask (the same prompt, schema, model and effort, sent through the product's client; at most 400 statements; ATT&CK group names, their short forms and spacing variants, and group ids hidden by the product's own rule) on each report's statements of at least three words with only the builder's actor masking (the names reading). The runner that feeds the set to this function is written before the freeze and its hash recorded in an amendment; it changes nothing in the function. It also reports the first-choice count with the model's first candidate as written (right only when candidate 1 itself is the right ATT&CK group): that is the number the block may state
arms.scorer: scripts/fresh_h2h_score.py --matching name --llm-min-probability 0.99 --switch-probability 0.5 (sha256 9fe424094274006d6cdb0920e40bcc1c54046956365706e42f091bcd1bfdf233), each model arm against the product run at its own reading; arms product, llm, llm_confident, switch, combination, agreed_or_confident. The model's candidates are matched by name only; its group ids are ignored. In this scorer the model's first choice is the first of its candidates that ATT&CK lists, read with the probability stated for its first candidate; the block shows the first candidate as written
arms.if_the_model_is_gone: if openai/gpt-5.6-sol is no longer served when a look is due, an amendment before any run names the replacement. A model whose knowledge cutoff lies inside the window cannot be tested on this set. The 0.99 cut-off was chosen for GPT-5.6 Sol's own numbers and does not carry over: for another model only the first-choice question is read, and its confident mark stays off in the product

hypotheses.primary_naming: behaviour reading, model_registered: llm_confident against product, wrong ATT&CK names in total (wrong names on known reports plus every name on the open set) and right names
hypotheses.primary_first_choice: behaviour reading, model_registered: switch against llm, right group first on known reports, paired bootstrap 95% interval (10,000 report resamples, seed 7) and exact McNemar
hypotheses.as_shipped: the same two comparisons for model_as_shipped against the product at the names reading, and the number of reports on which the two model arms give a different first choice or a different confident name
hypotheses.secondary: the model's first choice against the product's (llm against product); agreed_or_confident against llm_confident; the registered combination; right group in the model's first three; the id-first matching reported beside; names of actors outside ATT&CK counted separately; per-group macro first choice

reading_guide.naming: 'at least as safe' = llm_confident has no more wrong names in total than the product and at least as many right names; the share of right names is read with its exact 95% interval; with fewer than 10 confident names it is descriptive only (the guide of 2026-11-02)
reading_guide.first_choice: 'clearly ahead' = at least 0.10 higher with the bootstrap interval of the difference above 0; otherwise 'comparable' (the guide of 2026-10-28)
reading_guide.size: the first look (30-59 known reports) is descriptive only. The second look (60 or more) is the reading that counts; about 100 reports are needed to see a first-choice difference of 0.10, so 'comparable' at 60 is not evidence of no difference

consequence.now: the second opinion is in the product as an opt-in block, off by default (MODEL_OPINION_ENABLED), asked by a button, cloud model only: one request per click, which the product's client repeats once (a second paid request) when the answer is not valid JSON; the block then shows the second request's cost and tokens only. It shows the model's first choice as written, its stated probability, its decision and how it relates to the product's answer, and marks a 'confident name' by the rule above for the registered model and effort only. It is labelled as the model's own, uncalibrated answer
consequence.display_only: nothing from the second opinion enters classifier results, the fusion, the combiner (its fingerprint is unchanged), the naming gate, a confidence label or an export; it never runs during an analysis or a rescore. This holds whatever the result
consequence.wrong_confident_name: a confident name (llm_confident) that is wrong (a wrong name on a known report, or any name on an open-set report) on a report where the product does not give the same name
consequence.if_naming_fails: checked first, at either look (a one-sided stop; the first look is otherwise descriptive), in either model arm at its own reading: any wrong confident name as defined above. Then the 'confident name' mark is removed from the display (the answer and the stated probability stay, with the note) and the block stays off by default
consequence.if_naming_holds: otherwise, at the second look: llm_confident for model_registered at the behaviour reading is 'at least as safe' as the product with at least 10 confident names. Then the mark stays, and the product owner may decide to show the button by default where a cloud key is set
consequence.if_neither: otherwise (for example fewer than 10 confident names, all right): the mark stays as it is, the block stays off by default, and nothing is recommended. The three entries are exclusive and read in this order
consequence.first_choice: at the second look, switch against llm 'clearly ahead' for model_registered at the behaviour reading, and switch not behind llm for model_as_shipped at the names reading: the block may state the as-shipped arm's count of known reports on which the model's first candidate as written was the right group (n of N, with its exact 95% interval). Otherwise the block states no rate. The product's own first choice does not change; a switch that changes it stays the recommendation of llm_confidence_cutoff_2026-11-02 and needs the product owner's separate decision
consequence.limits: this file narrows the consequence of llm_confidence_cutoff_2026-11-02 for the confirmation set to the display; that file is unchanged. No default changes without the product owner

caveats: one sample per report; the model's probabilities are self-reported and coarse (many answers at exactly 0.99), and the product calls it without a seed, so a second click can give a different answer

a product case is not the tested text: with a cloud key the case statements are the extractor's rewritten actions, not report sentences, and only ATT&CK group names (with their short forms and spacing variants) and group ids are hidden, so vendor names ATT&CK does not list, most malware names, camel-case names split in two and the report's own attribution prose stay, while a capitalised ordinary word that is also an ATT&CK name is hidden too. The as-shipped arm reads report sentences with every actor name hidden by the builder, which is closer to the product than the behaviour reading but still not an analyst's case

the product's client sends the same question with different request fields (reasoning_effort, max_completion_tokens, no provider pinning, a retry on unreadable JSON) than the registered runner; the as-shipped arm exists to measure that call
labels are the vendors' attribution under the name-count rule; posts may retell research from before the model's cutoff; both systems know earlier reporting on the same actors
the two looks share reports; six confident names on the test of 2026-11-02 included three from one vendor's series on one group
cost: no credit for the registration or the product runs (local pipeline, GPU, about 30 minutes per reading). The model arms cost about 0.053-0.059 USD per report and arm (measured on 217 calls): about 8 USD at the first look (about 70 reports, two arms) and about 16 USD in total by the second (about 140 reports; cached answers are not paid twice). Each run is priced by a dry run with a cap before any spend. In the product each request costs about 0.05-0.06 USD (measured maximum 0.11); a repeated request costs again
